thirteen_lens_dispositions.bounded_assessment: The getter returns the existing typed rate; 95e AnimationFrequency admits finite positive hertz and AnimationSampleRate additionally checks a positive reciprocal duration. The native Duration boundary has its own explicit overflow/zero rejection, so leaf admission alone is not a universal guarantee of native clock representability.

Frequency and checked reciprocal are stored together privately by AnimationSampleRate and created together by TryFrom; no independent writable raw pair appears in this bounded type. Selected scenario time, clock interval and report playback are separate consumers whose relationship needs policy.

Historical P16 and current getter lines 88–92 are byte-identical; entire 267-line and 260-line file bodies differ, and unread differences are not characterized. No regression is inferred solely from revision or file hash.
Copy and serde through TryFrom/f32 preserve meaningful admission and source-frequency projection. No blanket claim that this checked serialization can be replaced by a derive-only raw structure.
No semantic boolean or payload-bearing enum occurs in the five-line getter. State of sample clock or selection across other files remains beyond this bounded read.

The getter returns AnimationSampleRate, and AnimationFrequency is deliberately weaker because it does not require a representable reciprocal. The native framework clock and report playback are consumers, not evidence for merging distinct rate owners.

Reciprocal and elapsed span conversion are explicit checked boundaries; conversion to native Duration separately rejects zero and overflow. Do not infer guaranteed successful native clock creation from finite positive f32 alone.

No raw numeric literal occurs in the scoped getter. Three turn scenarios use 64 normalized steps/time and HTML hardcodes 64-Hz playback; these connect to existing timestamp and display-policy questions, not a new counted issue.
No raw semantic string in the getter. Native clock exposes structured AnimationValueError; nearby report text uses a descriptive 64-Hz string, which is a display-policy question already retained.

The config stores sample_hz as AnimationSampleRate; runtime getter retrieves a copied animation snapshot and falls back to default initialization when no snapshot exists. The actual whole-system install order, cross-process propagation and every consumer are not demonstrated.

Current scenarios use normalized frame/64 as time for three turns while fixed logical elapsed and other scenario use the runtime rate; HTML uses 64 independently. Whether each is intended must be determined; connect, do not automatically merge, the existing records.

Frequency, sample rate with checked interval, elapsed and frame progress carry distinct contracts. The source makes it unsafe to interpret normalized turn progress as real elapsed at all rates without a policy-specific conversion.

AnimationSampleRate owns frequency/interval admission; configuration owns selected tuning; scenario and HTML each own a boundary use. Tuning must obey tactical-core AGENTS and the supported explicit runtime config, without assuming fixed-step networking has same rate authority.
